Topic: Introduction to Medicine and the Zimbabwean Health System
LearningOutcomes: Students will understand the organisation of Zimbabwe's health system, identify key institutions and policy frameworks, and recognise the major health challenges facing the country.
LectureTopics: The history of medicine and healthcare from ancient civilisations to modern practice
Structure of Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Care and service delivery levels
Major disease burdens in Zimbabwe: HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis, and non-communicable diseases
The role of the University of Zimbabwe College of Health Sciences in training healthcare professionals

Materials.Title: Introduction to Medicine and the Zimbabwean Health System - Lecture Slides
Introduction to Global Health - Video Overview

AssessmentMethods: Group discussion on health challenges in Zimbabwe and a short reflective writing exercise
FeedbackComments: Excellent introduction to the Zimbabwean health context. The use of current epidemiological data was highly effective.

LearningOutcomes: Students will apply the four principles of biomedical ethics to clinical scenarios, explain Zimbabwe's legal framework for patient rights, and demonstrate ethical reasoning in healthcare decision-making.
LectureTopics: The four principles of biomedical ethics: autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice
Informed consent: legal and ethical requirements under Zimbabwean law
Patient confidentiality, privacy rights, and the duty of care
Ethical dilemmas in clinical practice: resource allocation in low-income settings

Materials.Title: Medical Ethics and Patient Rights - Lecture Slides
Medical and Dental Practitioners Act Chapter 27:08 - Reference
Ethical Decision-Making in Clinical Practice - Notes

AssessmentMethods: Case-based ethical analysis exercise and class debate on resource allocation scenarios
FeedbackComments: Strong case-based approach to ethics. Students engaged thoughtfully with the resource allocation scenarios.

LearningOutcomes: Students will describe the double-helix structure of DNA, explain the semi-conservative model of DNA replication, and identify the key enzymes involved in the replication process.
LectureTopics: The double-helix model: Watson-Crick base pairing and the antiparallel structure of DNA
The semi-conservative model of DNA replication: evidence from the Meselson-Stahl experiment
Key enzymes in DNA replication: helicase, primase, DNA polymerase, and ligase
Replication fidelity, proofreading mechanisms, and common replication errors

Materials.Title: DNA Structure and Replication - Lecture Slides
Molecular Biology of the Cell - Chapter 5 Reference

AssessmentMethods: Diagram labelling exercise on DNA structure and short quiz on replication enzyme functions
FeedbackComments: Well-structured lecture with excellent visual aids. The animation resource will greatly aid student understanding.

LearningOutcomes: Students will identify and describe major pre-colonial kingdoms of southern Africa, analyse their political and economic structures, and evaluate their historical legacies.
LectureTopics: The Kingdom of Zimbabwe: Great Zimbabwe, stone architecture, and the Rozvi state
The Mutapa Empire: trade, gold, and interaction with the Swahili coast
The Ndebele Kingdom: origins, military organisation, and state formation
Pre-colonial social organisation, trade networks, and cultural achievements in southern Africa

Materials.Title: Pre-Colonial Kingdoms of Southern Africa - Lecture Slides
The African Past: Readings in African History - Reference
Great Zimbabwe: Archaeological Evidence - Video Documentary

AssessmentMethods: Map exercise identifying major southern African kingdoms and short essay on the historical significance of Great Zimbabwe
FeedbackComments: Excellent contextualisation of pre-colonial history. The inclusion of Great Zimbabwe as a local example is very effective.

LearningOutcomes: Students will define pathology and its subdisciplines, explain the cellular responses to injury and stress, and describe the basic mechanisms of acute and chronic inflammation.
LectureTopics: Overview of pathology: general, systemic, clinical, and forensic pathology
Cellular adaptations to stress: hypertrophy, hyperplasia, atrophy, and metaplasia
Cell injury and cell death: necrosis versus apoptosis
The inflammatory response: vascular changes, cellular events, and mediators of acute inflammation

Materials.Title: Introduction to Pathological Processes - Lecture Slides
Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease - Chapter 1 Reference
Cellular Adaptations to Injury - Lecture Notes

AssessmentMethods: Identification of pathological processes from histological slide images and short written response

LearningOutcomes: Students will apply kinematic equations to solve one-dimensional motion problems, explain Newton's three laws of motion with real-world examples, and calculate net force and acceleration in dynamic systems.
LectureTopics: Kinematics: displacement, velocity, acceleration, and kinematic equations for uniform motion
Newton's First Law: inertia and frames of reference
Newton's Second and Third Laws: force, mass, acceleration, and action-reaction pairs
Applications of Newton's laws: friction, tension, and inclined planes

Materials.Title: Mechanics - Motion and Forces Lecture Slides

AssessmentMethods: Problem-solving tutorial on kinematics and Newton's laws with peer review of solutions
